source.title: A Neural Collapse Perspective on Feature Evolution in Graph Neural Networks
source.authors: Vignesh Kothapalli; Tom Tirer; Joan Bruna

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests training and feature behavior in graph neural networks on stochastic block model graphs, an extension to node-wise graph classification. Its results do not test any listed version's specific CIFAR, teacher-student, depth/shortcut, initialization, learning-rate, or batch-normalization conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that trained GNNs reach zero training error (TPT), and describes within-class variability metrics decreasing and plateauing. These are results in a different model and task setting from the listed versions. Exact values in the training and NC1 plots are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study investigates neural collapse in GNN node classification and a graph-based unconstrained-features model. Its zero-training-error results concern SSBM graphs, outside V1's convolutional-network/CIFAR scope. Feature variability, graph-structure conditions and inference across layers do not measure any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the empirical conclusion correctly: GNN deepest features exhibit partial variability collapse, and variability metrics also decrease across layers during inference. Its theoretical summary needs qualification: condition C is sufficient for collapsed gUFM minimizers, while necessity is proved for a single graph under additional regularization, regularity and non-degeneracy assumptions. The unrestricted equivalence is conjectured. The authors argue that this rare structural condition helps explain incomplete collapse on practical graphs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses node-wise GNNs on SSBM graphs, MSE loss, instance normalization, and SGD; the initialization is not stated. It also studies a graph-based unconstrained-features model with plain gradient descent. These differ from the claim versions' CIFAR and other specified recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: For the graph-based unconstrained-features model, whether graphs satisfy condition C changes the reported NC1 outcome: significant reduction when satisfied, versus a plateau after reduction when not satisfied.

fits_no_version.finding: The tested GNNs reach zero training error on SSBM community-detection tasks while their penultimate-feature NC1 metrics decrease and plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GNNs can fit the tested SSBM node-classification datasets while exhibiting incomplete within-class feature collapse.

fits_no_version.finding: The graph-based unconstrained-features model shows much stronger NC1 reduction on constructed condition-C graphs than on graphs failing that condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Graph neighborhood structure affects the extent of feature collapse in the tested graph-based unconstrained-features model.

record.problems: Training overlap and NC1 plot values are not stated numerically in the text. The principal empirical experiments use a controlled SSBM setting; the paper describes results over graphs but does not give per-seed or per-graph outcome counts. The gUFM comparison uses 10 graphs per condition.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows beyond the extracted GNN and gUFM training and NC1 outcomes. Depthwise inference comparisons with spectral methods measure variability ratios rather than training classification error or a listed version's behavior.

untested.parts: CNN training error on CIFAR-10/100, including label corruption and model-size, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity residual shortcuts; the specified initialization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched, orthogonal or Gaussian initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because no row measures a listed version; this does not negate the reported GNN training success or NC1 changes. No additional result bearing on V1–V6 requires a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies node-wise GNN classification on SSBM graphs, not convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100; it does not test corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, or the listed regularized recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or width sweep.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or shortcut ablation.
No initialization comparison or initialization sweep.
No batch-normalization comparison; instance normalization is used in the GNN setup.
